sections.section_title: Structural Valve Deterioration and Serial TAVI Pathophysiology
sections.description: This section introduces the clinical background of structural heart disease following TAVI, explaining the natural decline of bioprosthetic valves and the unique physiological stressors introduced by valve-in-valve (VIV) configurations, specifically in triple valve scenarios.
subtopics: Mechanisms of bioprosthetic valve degeneration in TAVI patients over time
Pathophysiology of frame expansion, calcification, and leaflet stiffening in serial interventions
Specific haemodynamic challenges of TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV including reduced effective orifice area and coronary interference
Risk stratification of procedural complexity in triple-stented anatomy

sections.section_title: Clinical Evaluation, Diagnostic Criteria, and Indication Assessment
sections.description: This section guides the learner through the clinical journey from presenting symptoms to determining the intervention, focusing on how clinicians distinguish between anatomical failure, infection recurrence, and alternative management options like surgery.
subtopics: Symptom recognition in severe prosthetic valve dysfunction (symptoms, gradients, EF changes)
Diagnostic criteria for severe aortic stenosis and prosthetic valve endocarditis (Echo grading, haemodynamic thresholds)
Risk assessment frameworks: decision to bypass open surgery based on EuroSCORE and comorbidities
Integration of cardiac history (prior PVE) into the risk profile for subsequent interventions

sections.section_title: Advanced Imaging, Strategic Planning, and Device Selection
sections.description: This section details the multidisciplinary planning process prior to intervention, emphasizing the critical role of multidisciplinary heart team decisions, CT-guided planning, and the selection of specific devices to ensure safety and longevity.
subtopics: Pre-procedural multislice CT (MSCT) analysis for coronary protection (proximal valve height, coronary ostial clearance)
Strategic decision making: balancing surgical vs. catheter risk in high-comorbidity patients
Prosthetic sizing and deformation: selecting the Acurate neo2 for commissural alignment and hard/expansion ratio
Targeted imaging landmarks for ensuring frame-to-frame interaction does not compromise coronary flow

sections.description: This section provides a step-by-step analytical overview of the actual interventional procedure, illustrating the technical moves required to navigate complex anatomy and optimize immediate haemodynamic results.
subtopics: Access selection: femoral vs. radial arterial access and precautions
Shadowing facilities: balloon aortoplasty and rapid ventricular pacing rationale
Deployment technique: valve positioning, commissural alignment relative to leitiology
Verification of procedural success: immediate coronary angiography and flow assessment

sections.section_title: Long-Term Outcomes and Implications for Lifetime Valve Management
sections.description: This section evaluates the successful follow-up data against established metrics and synthesizes the clinical lessons for managing complex patients who require lifelong structural surveillance and iterative procedural planning.
subtopics: Standardized outcome measurement using Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC-3) criteria
Inter-vertex hemodynamic stability and durability assessment over 1-year follow-up
Clinical implications: balancing infection risk (PVE history) vs. mechanical valve failure risk
Strategies for lifelong monitoring of serial valve implantations and future access to surgical backup
